fixed-point.name: fractional bits

fixed-point.name: operation count
fixed-point.meaning: The number of operations applied since the layer began.

fixed-point.name: truncation
fixed-point.meaning: The single truncation that drops the bits below 2^{-p} in each real and imaginary part.

frequency-order.name: transform length

frequency-order.name: number of rounds

matrix-shear.name: digits per field

parameter-choice.quote: The lemmas bound $d,r,\ell$ by constants $a_d,a_r,b_d,b_r,C_\ell.$

parameter-choice.name: Gaussian width

phase-frames.name: address length

phase-frames.name: label

phase-frames.quote: Here $m$ is the number of binary coordinates of an address $x$, and a label $U$ is a subspace of $\mathbb F_2^m$.

phase-frames.name: complex wire count

phase-frames.name: column count

phase-frames.quote: For $k$ columns, let $Z_{a,k}$ be $Z$ on those 27 coordinates in every column.

phase-kernel.name: bit flip
phase-kernel.meaning: The 2x2 matrix that swaps the two entries of a pair.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ be the bit flip, which swaps the two entries of a pair $(u,v)$.

phase-kernel.name: kernel coefficient a
phase-kernel.meaning: The complex constant (1+i)/2, the coefficient of I in C.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $a=\frac{1+i}{2}$ and $b=\frac{1-i}{2}$ be two complex constants.

phase-kernel.name: kernel coefficient b
phase-kernel.meaning: The complex constant (1-i)/2, the coefficient of X in C.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $a=\frac{1+i}{2}$ and $b=\frac{1-i}{2}$ be two complex constants.

phase-kernel.name: two-point kernel
phase-kernel.meaning: The matrix aI + bX, a square root of the bit flip.
phase-kernel.quote: The kernel is $C=aI+bX$, where $I$ is the $2\times 2$ identity.

phase-kernel.name: phase matrix
phase-kernel.meaning: The diagonal matrix diag(1, i) that multiplies the second entry of a pair by i.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $\mathsf S=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ be the phase matrix that multiplies the second entry of a pair by $i$.

phase-kernel.name: butterfly matrix
phase-kernel.meaning: The matrix of the averaging and differencing step (u,v) -> ((u+v)/2, (u-v)/2).
phase-kernel.quote: Let $H_0=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ be the matrix of the averaging and differencing step $(u,v)\mapsto\bigl(\tfrac{u+v}{2},\tfrac{u-v}{2}\bigr)$.

phase-twist.name: last-axis variable
phase-twist.meaning: The variable of the last cyclic axis, with x_d^r = 1.
phase-twist.quote: Cyclic convolution along the last axis is multiplication in $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$, where $x_d$ is the variable of that axis and $x_d^r=1$.

phase-twist.name: twist phase
phase-twist.meaning: The number e^{\pi i/r}, a primitive 2r-th root of unity with \zeta^r = -1.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\zeta=e^{\pi i/r}$, a primitive $2r$-th root of unity, so $\zeta^r=-1$.

phase-twist.name: twist map
phase-twist.meaning: The ring isomorphism from C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1) to the negacyclic ring sending x_d to \zeta y.
phase-twist.quote: Define the ring map $\Theta$ from $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$ to $\mathcal R_r$ by $x_d\mapsto\zeta y$.

phase-twist.name: number of axes
phase-twist.meaning: The number of axes of the array f.
phase-twist.quote: Let a complex array $f$ have $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: total entries
phase-twist.meaning: The number of entries of the array f in all.
phase-twist.quote: Let a complex array $f$ have $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: number of records
phase-twist.meaning: The number of lines along the last axis, T/r.
phase-twist.quote: Then $M=T/r$ is the number of lines along the last axis.

phase-twist.name: record identification
phase-twist.meaning: Reads each line along the last axis as a polynomial in the negacyclic ring.
phase-twist.quote: The map $\iota$ reads each line $(f_{\boldsymbol j,k})_k$ as the polynomial $\sum_k f_{\boldsymbol j,k}y^k$, giving an array of $M$ records in $\mathcal R_r$.

phase-twist.name: diagonal twist
phase-twist.meaning: Multiplies entry k of each line by \zeta^{\pm k}.
phase-twist.quote: Let $(D_\pm f)_{\boldsymbol j,k}=\zeta^{\pm k}f_{\boldsymbol j,k}$ multiply entry $k$ of each line by $\zeta^{\pm k}$.

phase-twist.name: ring convolution
phase-twist.meaning: The ring convolution that convolves the first d-1 axes over the negacyclic ring and includes the division by T.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\mathcal M_r$ be the ring convolution of [Convolution from the retained transform layout](ring-convolution.md): it convolves the first $d-1$ axes over $\mathcal R_r$ and includes the division by $T$.

phase-twist.name: normalized cyclic convolution
phase-twist.meaning: The composite D_-\iota^{-1}\mathcal M_r(\iota D_+ f,\iota D_+ g), equal to f*g/T.
phase-twist.quote: Call the composite $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}$, the normalized complex cyclic convolution:

precision-recovery.name: digit width
precision-recovery.meaning: The number of bits in a radix digit.
precision-recovery.quote: Let $b$ be the bits per radix digit, $p=6b$ the fractional bits, $T$ the padded array size, $S\le T$ the convolution length, $L=\log_2T,$ $\gamma$ the source scale exponent, $d$ the axis count.

precision-recovery.name: fractional bits
precision-recovery.meaning: The number of fractional bits of the fixed-point grid, equal to $6b$.
precision-recovery.quote: Let $b$ be the bits per radix digit, $p=6b$ the fractional bits, $T$ the padded array size, $S\le T$ the convolution length, $L=\log_2T,$ $\gamma$ the source scale exponent, $d$ the axis count.

precision-recovery.name: padded array size
precision-recovery.meaning: The number of records in the padded array.
precision-recovery.quote: Let $b$ be the bits per radix digit, $p=6b$ the fractional bits, $T$ the padded array size, $S\le T$ the convolution length, $L=\log_2T,$ $\gamma$ the source scale exponent, $d$ the axis count.

precision-recovery.name: convolution length
precision-recovery.meaning: The length of the cyclic convolution.
precision-recovery.quote: Let $b$ be the bits per radix digit, $p=6b$ the fractional bits, $T$ the padded array size, $S\le T$ the convolution length, $L=\log_2T,$ $\gamma$ the source scale exponent, $d$ the axis count.

precision-recovery.name: log of T
precision-recovery.quote: Let $b$ be the bits per radix digit, $p=6b$ the fractional bits, $T$ the padded array size, $S\le T$ the convolution length, $L=\log_2T,$ $\gamma$ the source scale exponent, $d$ the axis count.

precision-recovery.name: source scale exponent
precision-recovery.meaning: The exponent of the source-transform scale $2^\gamma$.
precision-recovery.quote: Let $b$ be the bits per radix digit, $p=6b$ the fractional bits, $T$ the padded array size, $S\le T$ the convolution length, $L=\log_2T,$ $\gamma$ the source scale exponent, $d$ the axis count.

precision-recovery.name: axis count
precision-recovery.quote: Let $b$ be the bits per radix digit, $p=6b$ the fractional bits, $T$ the padded array size, $S\le T$ the convolution length, $L=\log_2T,$ $\gamma$ the source scale exponent, $d$ the axis count.

precision-recovery.name: grid step
precision-recovery.quote: Use $h_p=2^{-p}$ and the sup norm throughout; an error of $a$ means error less than $ah_p.$

precision-recovery.name: log of r
precision-recovery.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of the record length $r$.
precision-recovery.quote: Each synthetic transform has error less than $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}<L2^{-p}$ with $L=\log_2T,$ where $\ell=\log_2r.$

precision-recovery.name: ring record count
precision-recovery.meaning: The ratio $T/r$, the number of ring records.
precision-recovery.quote: With $M=T/r$ the ring record count, the ring convolution error is $E_{\rm ring}:=M(3L+2)<5TL,$ and its output has norm below $.701$ when one operand has norm at most $.7.$

precision-recovery.name: digit count
precision-recovery.meaning: The number of radix digits of an $n$-bit input.
precision-recovery.quote: We recover the coefficients $c_j$ of the [Multiplication as radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-reduction.md), which satisfy $c_j\le q(2^b-1)^2,$ with $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ the digits in an $n$-bit input.

radix-digit-reduction.name: first input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The first of the two integers being multiplied.

radix-digit-reduction.name: second input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The second of the two integers being multiplied.

radix-digit-reduction.name: input bit length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in each input.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each input, and let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the number of bits in one digit, so $n\le 2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit width
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in one radix digit.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each input, and let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the number of bits in one digit, so $n\le 2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: padded length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: A power of two with 4n/b <= T < 8n/b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $T$ is the padded length, a power of two with $4n/b\le T<8n/b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: convolution length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The length of the cyclic convolution, a product of distinct odd primes with T/2 < S < T.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $S$ is the length of the cyclic convolution, a product of distinct odd primes with $T/2<S<T$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit count
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of radix-2^b digits in each input.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ be the number of digits in each input, padding with leading zeros.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of u
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The i-th radix-2^b digit of u, an integer below 2^b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $v=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}v_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $v_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,v_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of v
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The k-th radix-2^b digit of v, an integer below 2^b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $v=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}v_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $v_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,v_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: polynomial variable
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The variable of the digit polynomials, evaluated at 2^b to recover the integers.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $x$ be a polynomial variable, and form the polynomials in $x$ with the $u_i$ and with the $v_k$ as coefficients.

radix-digit-reduction.name: product coefficient
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The coefficient of x^j in the product of the digit polynomials.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $c_j=\sum_{i+k=j}u_iv_k$ be the coefficient of $x^j$ in that product.

rank-recurrence.name: call parameter
rank-recurrence.meaning: The parameter of a call: the number of digits in each of the two interchanged chunks, or the number of axes the butterfly layer acts on.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call has a parameter $f$, the number of digits per interchanged chunk or of axes in the layer, and a volume $V$, the number of data symbols.

rank-recurrence.name: volume
rank-recurrence.meaning: The volume of a call: the number of data symbols it processes.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call has a parameter $f$, the number of digits per interchanged chunk or of axes in the layer, and a volume $V$, the number of data symbols.

rank-recurrence.name: block count
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of size-f blocks into which a call at parameter mf cuts its parameter, equal to 10^6 (also the dimension of the label space).
rank-recurrence.quote: A call at parameter $mf$, with $m=10^6$ the number of size-$f$ blocks in its parameter, splits its data into $W$ streams of volume $V/W$, one per wire of a fixed network with $W$ wires (bit-valued for interchange, complex for the layer).

rank-recurrence.name: wire count
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of wires of the fixed network, and so the number of streams a call splits its data into.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call at parameter $mf$, with $m=10^6$ the number of size-$f$ blocks in its parameter, splits its data into $W$ streams of volume $V/W$, one per wire of a fixed network with $W$ wires (bit-valued for interchange, complex for the layer).

rank-recurrence.name: number of smaller calls
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of calls at parameter f made by a call at parameter mf: the total rank of the frame changes over all edges of the network.
rank-recurrence.quote: So the call makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on volume $V/W$, where $s$ is the total rank over all edges, plus $O(V)$ other work.

rank-recurrence.name: normalized cost
rank-recurrence.meaning: F(f) is the running time of a call at parameter f divided by its volume.
rank-recurrence.quote: With $F(f)$ the time per unit volume of a call at parameter $f$, the children cost $s\,(V/W)\,F(f)$, so

rank-recurrence.name: recursion depth
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of levels of recursion: the number of factors m in a parameter m^k.
rank-recurrence.quote: Unrolling $k$ levels, with $k$ the number of factors $m$ in a parameter $m^k$, gives $F(m^k)=O\big(\sum_{j=0}^{k}(s/W)^j\big)$.

rank-recurrence.name: saving exponent
rank-recurrence.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 with s/W < m^tau, which makes a call cost O(V f^tau); here tau = 1 - 2^{-50}.
rank-recurrence.quote: If $s/W<m^\tau$ for a fixed exponent $\tau<1$, the sum is $O(m^{k\tau})$: at most $k+1$ when $s/W\le1$, and $O((s/W)^k)$ otherwise.

rank-recurrence.name: relative deficit
rank-recurrence.meaning: The fraction (Wm - s)/(Wm) by which the number of smaller calls s falls short of Wm.
rank-recurrence.quote: Write $s/W=m(1-\eta)$, where $\eta=(Wm-s)/(Wm)$ is the relative deficit, equal to $339/22587335000000$ for the bit network and $73/19906842167500$ for the complex one

retained-permutations.name: number of axes
retained-permutations.quote: Take $d$ axes with pairwise coprime prime lengths $s_i$ and power-of-two lengths $t_i>s_i$.

retained-permutations.name: prime length
retained-permutations.meaning: The prime length of axis i.
retained-permutations.quote: Take $d$ axes with pairwise coprime prime lengths $s_i$ and power-of-two lengths $t_i>s_i$.

retained-permutations.name: power-of-two length
retained-permutations.meaning: The power-of-two length of axis i.
retained-permutations.quote: Take $d$ axes with pairwise coprime prime lengths $s_i$ and power-of-two lengths $t_i>s_i$.

retained-permutations.name: product of prime lengths
retained-permutations.meaning: The product of the prime lengths.
retained-permutations.quote: Let $F_{\boldsymbol q}=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ be the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) along every axis, $F_{\boldsymbol q}^+$ its opposite, $S=\prod_is_i$ and $T=\prod_it_i$.

retained-permutations.name: padded box size
retained-permutations.meaning: The number of entries in the padded box, the product of the power-of-two lengths.
retained-permutations.quote: Let $F_{\boldsymbol q}=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ be the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) along every axis, $F_{\boldsymbol q}^+$ its opposite, $S=\prod_is_i$ and $T=\prod_it_i$.

retained-permutations.name: bit precision
retained-permutations.meaning: The number of bits of precision of each coordinate.
retained-permutations.quote: Let $p$ be the bit precision of each coordinate, $\alpha$ an integer width of the Gaussian weights, and $\delta$ a fixed exponent.

retained-permutations.name: Gaussian width
retained-permutations.meaning: An integer width parameter of the Gaussian weights.
retained-permutations.quote: Let $p$ be the bit precision of each coordinate, $\alpha$ an integer width of the Gaussian weights, and $\delta$ a fixed exponent.

retained-permutations.name: time exponent
retained-permutations.meaning: A fixed exponent in the time bound.
retained-permutations.quote: Let $p$ be the bit precision of each coordinate, $\alpha$ an integer width of the Gaussian weights, and $\delta$ a fixed exponent.

retained-permutations.name: source permutation
retained-permutations.meaning: The source coordinate permutation, tensor product of the one-axis permutations P_{s_i}.
retained-permutations.quote: Tensoring over the axes, put $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$.

retained-permutations.name: target permutation
retained-permutations.meaning: The target coordinate permutation, tensor product of the one-axis permutations P_{t_i}.
retained-permutations.quote: Tensoring over the axes, put $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$.

retained-permutations.name: chunk width
retained-permutations.meaning: The width in bits of the chunks swapped.
retained-permutations.quote: Exposing each axis as the innermost field uses the [fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md), which swaps chunks of $w$ bits within $V$ bits in $O(Vw^\tau)$ time for a fixed $\tau<1$.

retained-permutations.name: total bits
retained-permutations.meaning: The total number of bits within which chunks are swapped.
retained-permutations.quote: Exposing each axis as the innermost field uses the [fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md), which swaps chunks of $w$ bits within $V$ bits in $O(Vw^\tau)$ time for a fixed $\tau<1$.

retained-permutations.name: chunk-swap exponent
retained-permutations.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the chunk-swap time bound.
retained-permutations.quote: Exposing each axis as the innermost field uses the [fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md), which swaps chunks of $w$ bits within $V$ bits in $O(Vw^\tau)$ time for a fixed $\tau<1$.

ring-convolution.name: number of records
ring-convolution.meaning: The number of polynomial records, one per cyclic address of the remaining axes.
ring-convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_i t_i$ be the number of records, $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients, and $*$ cyclic convolution.

ring-convolution.name: number of coefficients
ring-convolution.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in an array, T = rM.
ring-convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_i t_i$ be the number of records, $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients, and $*$ cyclic convolution.

ring-convolution.name: log of record length
ring-convolution.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of the record length r.
ring-convolution.quote: Each transform costs $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$, where $\ell=\log_2r$, $K$ is the layout chunk width, and $\tau,\lambda'$ are exponents from the cost lemma.

ring-convolution.name: layout chunk width
ring-convolution.meaning: The width of the address chunks used by the tape layout.
ring-convolution.quote: Each transform costs $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$, where $\ell=\log_2r$, $K$ is the layout chunk width, and $\tau,\lambda'$ are exponents from the cost lemma.

ring-convolution.name: pointwise product
ring-convolution.meaning: The pointwise product of records, P(u,v) = uv/r.

ring-convolution.name: transform error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * l * 2^{-p} for each forward transform.
ring-convolution.quote: Put $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ for each forward transform error and $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ for one truncation.

ring-convolution.name: truncation error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * 2^{-p} for one truncation.
ring-convolution.quote: Put $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ for each forward transform error and $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ for one truncation.

ring-y.name: ring variable
ring-y.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials, satisfying y^r = -1 in the ring.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

ring-y.name: record length
ring-y.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

signed-packing.name: precision bits
signed-packing.meaning: The number of fractional bits in each coefficient component.
signed-packing.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits in each coefficient component, with $r<2^p$.

signed-packing.name: packing base
signed-packing.meaning: The power of two $2^{4p}$ at which the polynomials are evaluated.

signed-packing.name: evaluation integer
signed-packing.meaning: The signed integer obtained by evaluating the polynomial u at B_0.
signed-packing.quote: For $u\in\{a,b,c,e\}$ let $A_u=u(B_0)=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}u_jB_0^j$ be the signed evaluation integer.

signed-packing.name: numerator coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The Gaussian integer coefficient of y^j after reduction modulo y^r+1.
signed-packing.quote: Let $H_j$ be the resulting Gaussian integer coefficient of $y^j$.

simultaneous-layer.name: stream volume
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of bits of the stream.
simultaneous-layer.quote: On a stream of $V$ bits, with address chunks of $K$ bits and coefficients of $p$ fractional bits, the simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0(u,v)=\bigl(\tfrac{u+v}2,\tfrac{u-v}2\bigr)$ to one bit in each of $D\le d$ chunks in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),\ \lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ whole-array passes.

simultaneous-layer.name: chunk width
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of bits in an address chunk.
simultaneous-layer.quote: On a stream of $V$ bits, with address chunks of $K$ bits and coefficients of $p$ fractional bits, the simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0(u,v)=\bigl(\tfrac{u+v}2,\tfrac{u-v}2\bigr)$ to one bit in each of $D\le d$ chunks in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),\ \lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ whole-array passes.

simultaneous-layer.name: fractional bits
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of fractional bits of each coefficient.
simultaneous-layer.quote: On a stream of $V$ bits, with address chunks of $K$ bits and coefficients of $p$ fractional bits, the simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0(u,v)=\bigl(\tfrac{u+v}2,\tfrac{u-v}2\bigr)$ to one bit in each of $D\le d$ chunks in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),\ \lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ whole-array passes.

The layout permutation $L$, built below, adds one record permutation to the [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md): the forward entry with frequency address $j$ is stored at $L(Bj)$.
